|lang2=[[Armenian numerals|Armenian]]|lang2 symbol=Օ|lang3=[[Egyptian numerals|Egyptian hieroglyph]]|lang3 symbol=<span style="font-size:300%;">𓂭</span>|divisor=25 total}}

'''10,000''' ('''ten thousand''') is the [[natural number]] following [[9999 (number)|9,999]] and preceding 10,001.

==Name==
{{See also|Orders of magnitude (numbers)}}

Many languages have a specific word for this number; in [[Ancient Greek]] it is {{lang|grc|μύριοι}} (the etymological root of the word [[myriad]] in [[English language|English]]), in [[Aramaic language|Aramaic]] {{lang|arc|ܪܒܘܬܐ}}, in [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] {{lang|he|רבבה}} [{{transliteration|he|revava}}], in [[Chinese language|Chinese]] {{lang|zh|萬/万}} (Mandarin {{transliteration|cmn|wàn}}, [[Cantonese]] {{transliteration|yue|maan6}}, Hokkien ''bān''), in [[Japanese language|Japanese]] {{nihongo2|万/萬}} [{{transliteration|ja|man}}], in [[Khmer language|Khmer]] {{lang|km|ម៉ឺន}} [{{transliteration|km|meun}}], in [[Korean language|Korean]] {{lang|ko|만/萬}} [{{transliteration|ko|man}}], in [[Russian language|Russian]] {{lang|ru|тьма}} [{{transliteration|ru|t'ma}}], in [[Vietnamese language|Vietnamese]] {{lang|vi|vạn}}, in [[Sanskrit]] अयुत [''ayuta''], in [[Thai language|Thai]] {{lang|th|หมื่น}} [{{transliteration|th|meun}}], in [[Malayalam]] {{lang|ml|പതിനായിരം}} [{{transliteration|ml|patinayiram}}], and in [[Malagasy language|Malagasy]] ''alina''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://malagasyword.org/bins/teny2/alina|title = Malagasy Dictionary and Madagascar Encyclopedia : Alina}}</ref> In many of these languages, it often denotes a [[indefinite and fictitious numbers|very large but indefinite number]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/myriad|title=Myriad Definition & Meaning - Merriam-Webster|website=Merriam-Webster's Online Dictionary|date=13 March 2024 }}</ref>

The classical [[Greeks]] used letters of the [[Greek alphabet]] to represent [[Greek numerals]]: they used a capital letter [[Mu (letter)|mu]] (Μ) to represent ten thousand.{{Citation needed|date=February 2024}} This Greek root was used in early versions of the [[metric system]] in the form of the decimal prefix [[Non-SI unit prefix|myria-]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Baldwin |first=James |date=1885 |title=Notes on Teaching History |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/44009109 |journal=Educational Weekly |volume=5 |issue=2 |pages=4–5 |jstor=44009109 |issn=2475-3262}}</ref>

Depending on the country, the number ten thousand is usually written as 10,000 (including in the UK and US), 10.000, or 10 000.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E19455-01/806-0169/overview-9/index.html|title=Decimal and Thousands Separators (International Language Environments Guide)|website=oracle.com}}</ref>

==In mathematics==
In [[scientific notation]], it is written as '''10<sup>4</sup>''' or '''1 E+4''' (equivalently '''1 E4''') in [[E notation]]. It is the [[Square (algebra)|square]] of [[100 (number)|100]] and the [[square root]] of [[100,000,000]].

The value of a [[myriad]] to the [[Exponentiation|power]] of itself, 10000<sup>10000</sup> = 10<sup>40000</sup>.

It has a [[Carmichael function|reduced totient]] of [[1000 (number)|500]], and a [[Euler's totient function|totient]] of [[4000 (number)|4,000]], with a total of 16 [[integer]]s having a totient value of 10,000.<ref>{{Cite OEIS |A002322 |Reduced totient function}}</ref><ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000010|Euler totient function}}</ref>

There are a total of [[1229 (number)|1,229]] prime numbers less than ten thousand, a count that is itself prime.<ref name=A006880>{{Cite OEIS|A006880|Number of primes less than 10^n}}</ref><ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000040|The prime numbers}} See "Table of n, prime(n) for n = 1..10000" under "Links".</ref> 
 
A [[myriagon]] is a [[polygon]] with '''ten thousand edges''' and a total of 25 [[dihedral group|dihedral]] symmetry groups when including the myriagon itself, alongside  25 [[cyclic group]]s as [[subgroup]]s.<ref>{{Cite book |author1=John Horton Conway |author1-link= John Horton Conway |author2=Heidi Burgiel |author3=Chaim Goodman-Strauss |url=https://www.routledge.com/The-Symmetries-of-Things/Conway-Burgiel-Goodman-Strauss/p/book/9781568812205 |title=The Symmetries of Things |publisher=[[A K Peters|A K Peters/CRC Press]] |year=2008 |isbn=978-1-56881-220-5 }} Chapter 20.</ref>

* In [[climate]], '''Summary of 10000 Years''' is one of several pages of the ''Climate Timeline Tool: Exploring Weather & Climate Change Through the Powers of 10'' sponsored by the [[National Climatic Data Center]] of the [[National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120805071442/http://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/paleo/ctl/index.html|title=Climate Timeline Information Tool}}</ref>
* In [[computing]],
** [[65,536]] [[kilobyte]]s in [[decimal]] is equal to '''10,000 kB''' in [[hexadecimal]] (the equivalent [[Addressing mode|addressing]] ranges of 0 to [[65,535]] in decimal are 0 to FFFF in hex).
**[[NASA]] built a '''10000-processor [[Linux]] computer''' (it is actually a 10,240-processor) called [[Columbia (supercomputer)|Columbia]].<ref>[http://www.infoworld.com/article/04/07/28/HNnasalinux_1.html news]</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nas.nasa.gov/About/Projects/Columbia/columbia.html |title=NASA Project: Columbia |access-date=2005-02-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050408085108/http://www.nas.nasa.gov/About/Projects/Columbia/columbia.html |archive-date=2005-04-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* In [[geography]],
**'''Land of 10000 Lakes''' is the [[nickname]] for the state of [[Minnesota]].
** '''Land of 10000 Trails''' or '''10000trails.com''' is an organization created in 1999 by the TN/KY Lakes Area Coalition and based in West [[Tennessee]] and West [[Kentucky]] to promote tourism by developing trails in the region.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20010517233545/http://www.10000trails.com/ 10000 trails web site]}}</ref>
** '''[[Ten Thousand Islands National Wildlife Refuge]]''' is situated in the lower end of the Fakahatchee and Picayune Strands of [[Big Cypress Swamp]] and west of [[Everglades National Park]] in [[Florida]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://southeast.fws.gov/TenThousandIsland/ |title=Ten Thousand Islands NWR |website=U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service |access-date=2005-02-14 |archive-date=2005-03-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050301104852/http://southeast.fws.gov/tenthousandisland/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
** '''[[Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes]]''' in [[Alaska]].
* In [[physics]],
** [[Myria-]] (and [[myrio-]])<ref name="Brewster_1830">{{cite book|title=The Edinburgh Encyclopædia|first=David|last=Brewster|volume=12|date=1830|location=Edinburgh, UK|publisher=William Blackwood, John Waugh, John Murray, Baldwin & Cradock, J. M. Richardson|page=494|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0bIkTUZAbxcC|access-date=2015-10-09}}</ref><ref name="Brewster_1832">{{cite book|title=The Edinburgh Encyclopaedia|first=David|last=Brewster|volume=12|edition=1st American|date=1832|publisher=Joseph and Edward Parker<!-- |printer=William Brows -->|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=17RGAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA572|access-date=2015-10-09}}</ref><ref name="Dingler_1823">{{cite book|title=Polytechnisches Journal|first=Johann Gottfried|last=Dingler|volume=11|date=1823|publisher=J.W. Gotta'schen Buchhandlung|language=de|location=Stuttgart, Germany|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wF3zAAAAMAAJ&pg=PA500|access-date=2015-10-09}}</ref> is an obsolete [[metric prefix]] that denoted a factor of '''10<sup>+4</sup>''', '''ten thousand''', or '''10,000'''.
** '''10,000 [[hertz]], 10 [[kilohertz]]'', or ''10&nbsp;kHz''' of the [[radio frequency]] spectrum falls in the [[very low frequency]] or VLF band and has a [[wavelength]] of 30 kilometres.
** In [[orders of magnitude (speed)]], the [[speed]] of a [[fast neutron]] is '''10000&nbsp;km/s'''.
** In [[acoustics]], '''10,000 [[hertz]], 10 [[kilohertz]]'', or ''10&nbsp;kHz''' of a sound signal at sea level has a wavelength of about 34&nbsp; mm.
** In [[music]], a 10 kilohertz sound is a [[E♭ (musical note)|E♭<sub>9</sub>]] in the [[A440 (pitch standard)|A440 pitch standard]], a bit more than an octave higher in pitch than the highest note on a standard piano.

==In time==
* '''10000 BC''', '''10000 BCE''', or '''[[10th millennium BC]].'''
* '''10000-year clock''' or the [[Clock of the Long Now]] is a mechanical clock designed to keep time for 10000 years.

==In other fields==
* In currency,
** A version of [[Iraq]]'s 10,000 [[Iraqi dinar|dinar]] [[banknote]] has Abu Ali Hasan Ibn al-Haitham (also known as [[Alhazen]]) on the front, and a later issue has sculptor [[Jawad Saleem]]'s Freedom Monument in Baghdad on the front. Both notes have an image of Mosul's [[Great Mosque of al-Nuri (Mosul)#Minaret|al-Hadba' Minaret]] on the back.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iraqi-dinar.com/dinar-currency.php |title=Iraq Dinar Currency Photos&#124; Banknote Series &#124; 25000, 10000, 5000, 1000, 250, 50 Dinars |publisher=iraqi-dinar.com |date= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050207025025/http://www.iraqi-dinar.com/dinar-currency.php |access-date=2022-08-04|archive-date=2005-02-07 }}</ref> The first issue had an image of former Iraqi president [[Saddam Hussein]] and the Spiral Minaret - [[Malwiya minaret|Al-Minārat Al-Malwiyyah]] in [[Samarra]].<ref>http://www.iraqsales.com/10%2C000.htm {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050206094238/http://iraqsales.com/10,000.htm |date=2005-02-06 }}</ref>
** the Japanese [[Japanese yen|¥]]10,000 banknote depicts [[Fukuzawa Yukichi]].
** [[Kazakhstan]]'s 10,000[[Kazakhstani tenge|₸]] banknote.
** the [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] [[Lebanese pound|£L]]10,000 banknote depicts Beirut's [[Martyrs' Square, Beirut|Martyrs' Square]].
** [[Myanmar]]'s (Burma's) [[Burmese kyat|Ks.]]10,000/- banknote.
** the U.S. [[Large denominations of United States currency|$10,000 note]] depicts a picture of [[Salmon P. Chase]].
* In distances,
** 10&nbsp;km, 10,000 m, or [[1 E+4 m]] is equal to:
*** 1 Scandinavian [[Scandinavian mile|''mil'']].
*** about 6.2137 [[mile|English miles]].
*** side of [[Square (geometry)|square]] with area [[Orders of magnitude (area)|100]] km<sup>2</sup>.
*** radius of a [[circle]] with area 100 '''{{pi}}''' km<sup>2</sup> ≈ 314.159&nbsp;km<sup>2</sup>.
* In finance, on March 29, 1999, the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] closed at 10006.78, which was the first time the index closed above the 10,000 mark.
* In [[futurology]], [[Stewart Brand]] in ''Visions of the Future: The 10,000-Year Library'' proposes a museum built around a 10,000-year clock as an idea for assuring that vital information survives future crashes of civilizations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kurzweilai.net/meme/frame.html?main=%2Farticles%2Fart0158.html |title=	The 10,000-Year Library |first=Stewart |last=Brand |website=kurzweilai.net |date= |archive-url=	https://web.archive.org/web/20050205055351/http://www.kurzweilai.net/meme/frame.html?main=%2Farticles%2Fart0158.html |access-date=2022-08-04|archive-date=2005-02-05 }}</ref>
* In games,
** ''Ten Thousand'' is one name of a dice game called [[farkle]].
* In game shows, ''[[Pyramid (game show)|The $10,000 Pyramid]]'' ran on television from 1973 to 1974.
* In history,
**'' [[Army of 10,000]]'' Mississippi [[American Civil War]] military unit, 1861–1862.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mississippiscv.org/MS_Units/army_of_10k.htm |title=Army of 10,000 |website=mississippiscv.org |date= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20020401045041/http://mississippiscv.org/MS_Units/army_of_10k.htm |access-date=2022-08-04|archive-date=2002-04-01 }}</ref>
** The ''[[Army of the Ten Thousand]]'' were a group of [[Ancient Greek]] [[mercenaries]] who marched against [[Artaxerxes II of Persia]].
** The [[Persian Immortals]] were also called the ''Ten Thousand'' or ''10,000 Immortals'', so named because their Number of 10,000 was immediately re-established after every loss.
** ''The 10,000 Day War: Vietnam'' by [[Michael Maclear]] {{ISBN|0-312-79094-5}}  also alternate titles ''The ten thousand day war: Vietnam, 1945–1975'' (10,000 days is 27.4 years).
** ''Tomb of Ten Thousand Soldiers'' – defeat of the [[Tang dynasty]] army of China in the [[Kingdom of Nanzhao|Nanzhao]] kingdom in 751.
** In Islamic history, 10,000 is the Number of besieging forces led by Muhammad's adversary, [[Abu Sufyan]], during the [[Battle of the Trench]].
** 10,000 is the number of [[Muhammad]]'s soldiers during the [[conquest of Mecca]].
* In [[language]],
** the Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Vietnamese phrase ''[[ten thousand years|live for ten thousand years]]'' was used to bless emperors in East Asia.
** [[Myriad|Μύριοι]] is an [[Ancient Greek]] name for 10.000 taken into the modern European languages as 'myriad' (see above). Hebrew, Chinese, Japanese, and Korean have words with the same meaning.
* In literature,
** {{Lang|ja-latn|[[Man'yōshū]]}} ({{nihongo2|万葉集}} {{Lang|ja-latn|Man'yōshū}}, ''Collection of Ten Thousand Leaves'') is the oldest existing, and most highly revered, collection of [[Japanese poetry]].
** ''Ten Thousand a Year'' 1839 by [[Samuel Warren (British lawyer)|Samuel Warren]].
** ''Ten Thousand a Year'' 1883?. A drama in three acts. Adapted from the celebrated novel of the same name, by the author of the ''Diary of a Physician'', and arranged for the stage by [[Richard Brinsley Peake]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hti.umich.edu/cgi/b/bib/bibperm?q1=eprosed-P3.0504 | title=University of Michigan Digital Library - Login Options }}</ref>
** [[Anabasis (Xenophon)|Anabasis]], by the Greek writer Xenophon (431–360 B.C.), about the ''[[Army of the Ten Thousand]]'' – Greek mercenaries taking part in the expedition of Cyrus the Younger, a Persian prince, against his brother, King Artaxerxes II.
** ''The Ten Thousand: A Novel of Ancient Greece'' by [[Michael Curtis Ford]]. 2001. {{ISBN|0-312-26946-3}}  Historic fiction about the ''[[Army of the Ten Thousand]]''.
** ''The World of the Ten Thousand Things: Poems 1980&ndash;1990'' by [[Charles Wright (poet)|Charles Wright]]  {{ISBN|0-374-29293-0}}  {{ISBN|0-374-52326-6}}.
** ''Ten Thousand Lovers'' by [[Edeet Ravel]] {{ISBN|0-06-056562-4}}.
* In philosophy, [[Lao Zi]] writes about ''ten thousand things'' in the [[Tao Te Ching]]. In [[Taoism]], the "10,000 Things" is a term meaning all of phenomenal [[reality]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebigview.com/tao-te-ching/chapter34.html |title=Tao Te Ching, Verse 34 |website=thebigview.com |date= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070817180923/http://www.thebigview.com/tao-te-ching/chapter34.html |access-date=2022-08-04|archive-date=2007-08-17 }}</ref>
* In [[piphilology]], ten thousand is the current world record for the Number of digits of [[pi]] memorized by a human being.
* In psychology, ''Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted'', or what's in a [[dream]]: a scientific and practical, by Miller, Gustavus Hindman (1857–1929). [[Project Gutenberg]].<ref>https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/926 : Ten Thousand Dreams Interpreted</ref>
* In religion,
** The [[Bible]],
*** has 52 references to ten thousand in the [[King James Version]].<ref>http://bible.gospelcom.net/keyword/?search=ten%20thousand&version1=9&searchtype=phrase&wholewordsonly=yes , [http://bible.gospelcom.net/keyword/?search=ten%20thousands&version1=9&searchtype=phrase]</ref>
*** [[Book of Revelation|Revelation]] 5:11 ''And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands''.<ref>[http://www.earlychristianwritings.com/text/revelation-kjv.html (KJV)] [http://www.earlychristianwritings.com/revelation.html The Apocalypse of John]</ref>
** [[hymn]], ''Ten thousand times ten thousand''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hymnary.org/text/ten_thousand_times_ten_thousand_in_spark|title=Ten Thousand Times Ten Thousand|website=Hymnary.org}}</ref>
** The [[Ten thousand martyrs]].<ref>[https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/09746a.htm ''The Catholic Encyclopedia'']</ref>
* In software,
** The ''[[Year 10,000 problem]]'' is the collective name for all potential software bugs that will emerge as the need to express years with five digits arises.
* In sports,
** In athletics, ''10,000 meters'', ''10 kilometers'', ''10 km'', or ''10K'' (6.2 miles) is the final standard track event in a [[long-distance track event]] and a distance in other [[racing]] events such as [[running]], [[cycle sport|cycling]], and [[skiing]].
** In bicycle racing, annual ''Tour of 10,000 Lakes Stage Race'' in [[Minneapolis]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeanne|last=Ulmer |url=http://www.tourof10000lakes.net/ |title=Minnesota Cycling Team –Tour of 10,000 Lakes |website=tourof10000lakes.net |date= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050221101850/http://www.tourof10000lakes.net/ |access-date=2022-08-04|archive-date=2005-02-21 }}</ref>
** In baseball, on July 15, 2007, the [[Philadelphia Phillies]] became the first team in American professional sports history to lose 10,000 games.

===Primes===
There are [[1033 (number)|1033]] prime numbers between 10000 and 20000, a count that is itself prime. It is [[196 (number)|196]] prime numbers less than the number of primes between 0 and 10000 ([[1229 (number)|1229]], also prime).
